bug_semantics: When an application configures allowedAud, allowedIss, allowedSub, allowedJti, or allowedNonce with a backtracking-prone RegExp, fast-jwt retains that RegExp as the claim matcher and invokes its .test() method on the corresponding attacker-controlled JWT claim after signature verification. A validly signed token containing an adversarial non-matching string can therefore cause exponential JavaScript-regex backtracking, block the Node.js event loop, and exhaust CPU. String allow-list entries, safe regular expressions, and default configurations do not trigger this mechanism.
flaw_origin: The smallest introducing change is the initial verifier implementation in 51fe1ea3feacb931cd66b0f915b046cbeab88790. It created src/verifier.js, accepted any supplied matcher having a test function (therefore retaining RegExp objects), applied allowed matchers directly with a.test(value), and wired all five allowed* options to attacker-controlled claims. Its direct parent 5063678a36ff118da9671f1f1df3d67cc95d1169 had no src/verifier.js or equivalent verifier implementation. Later changes altered exact-string handling and reset stateful RegExp.lastIndex, but preserved the unsafe application-supplied RegExp execution and are not the BIC.
ai_marker: absent — the raw BIC commit object identifies author and committer as Shogun <shogun@cowtech.it>, has the sole message "feat(wip): Initial version.", contains no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, or other AI trailer, and neither identity is a bot.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/nearform/fast-jwt/security/advisories/GHSA-cjw9-ghj4-fwxf identifies the authenticated CPU-exhaustion path, the affected configuration and example /^(a+)+X$/, declared affected versions >=5.0.0 through <=6.2.0, and patched version 6.2.1. It states that the attacker-controlled aud claim is evaluated by the configured RegExp after signature validation.

BIC commit and source: https://github.com/nearform/fast-jwt/commit/51fe1ea3feacb931cd66b0f915b046cbeab88790 and https://github.com/nearform/fast-jwt/blob/51fe1ea3feacb931cd66b0f915b046cbeab88790/src/verifier.js#L6-L11. The new ensureStringClaimMatcher returns a supplied object whenever it has a test function, retaining a supplied RegExp. Lines 30-58 (https://github.com/nearform/fast-jwt/blob/51fe1ea3feacb931cd66b0f915b046cbeab88790/src/verifier.js#L30-L58) call a.test(value) on a JWT claim; lines 138-155 wire allowedJti, allowedAud, allowedIss, allowedSub, and allowedNonce; lines 167-176 show algorithm/signature verification precedes payload validation.

History proof: git log -L on src/verifier.js traced ensureStringClaimMatcher to 51fe1ea3feacb931cd66b0f915b046cbeab88790. Pickaxe for "function ensureStringClaimMatcher" found that same earliest commit. The commit adds src/verifier.js as a new file from /dev/null rather than moving or refactoring existing code. A later exact-string fix, b1d71ed6dd54796099e8bccc18543d4c731b1746, continued returning application objects with a test method; v6.2.0 still returns the supplied RegExp at src/verifier.js:47-48 and invokes it at src/verifier.js:163.

Direct-parent verification: git ls-tree -r 5063678a36ff118da9671f1f1df3d67cc95d1169 -- src/verifier.js returned no entry, while the parent tree contained only repository metadata/configuration files, CHANGELOG, package.json, and yarn.lock. The parent commit is https://github.com/nearform/fast-jwt/commit/5063678a36ff118da9671f1f1df3d67cc95d1169; the BIC diff shows src/verifier.js as new file mode 100644 from /dev/null. Thus the vulnerable matcher and invocation are absent in the immediate parent.

Version-boundary proof: git merge-base --is-ancestor 51fe1ea3feacb931cd66b0f915b046cbeab88790 v5.0.0 exited 0, and git tag --contains the BIC includes v0.1.0 onward, including v5.0.0 and v6.2.0, so the BIC predates the advisory's lower bound. Tag v5.0.0 resolves to release commit 72f91b547f5dca90715a70ff3cbaa042e40d8803; v6.2.0 resolves to e07b1fd23f02a47f1be677a21a4f07607b478e66. The advisory's >=5.0.0 boundary is therefore a declared support/assessment boundary, not the historical introduction of the mechanism.

Official fix evidence: https://github.com/nearform/fast-jwt/commit/b0be0ca161593836a153d5180ca5358ad9b5de94 (PR https://github.com/nearform/fast-jwt/pull/595) adds safe-regex2, checkForUnsafeRegExp at src/verifier.js:41-52, and construction-time checks for all five allowed* options at lines 537-541. git tag --contains b0be0ca161593836a153d5180ca5358ad9b5de94 starts at v6.2.1; it does not include v6.2.0. Release commit 6b13fe96614a38613d453f46ba0631c4cd09dcd8 has b0be0ca161593836a153d5180ca5358ad9b5de94 as its direct parent and is tagged v6.2.1: https://github.com/nearform/fast-jwt/releases/tag/v6.2.1. git merge-base --is-ancestor b0be0ca161593836a153d5180ca5358ad9b5de94 v6.2.1 exited 0.

Fix-semantics caveat: the final b0be0ca161593836a153d5180ca5358ad9b5de94 code emits FAST_JWT_UNSAFE_REGEXP via process.emitWarning but does not reject, rewrite, or stop registration of the unsafe RegExp; the existing matcher can still call r.test(v). Thus b0be0ca161593836a153d5180ca5358ad9b5de94 is the advisory-designated direct fix and version-boundary commit, but its final source implements detection/warning rather than the PR description's claimed eager rejection.

BIC-only attribution proof: numactl-prefixed git show --format=raw 51fe1ea3feacb931cd66b0f915b046cbeab88790 shows parent 5063678a36ff118da9671f1f1df3d67cc95d1169, human author/committer Shogun <shogun@cowtech.it>, and only the message "feat(wip): Initial version." No commit-object AI marker or bot identity is present: https://github.com/nearform/fast-jwt/commit/51fe1ea3feacb931cd66b0f915b046cbeab88790.
reasoning: The advisory's causal requirement is an application-supplied unsafe RegExp plus an attacker-controlled claim in a validly signed JWT. Source history establishes that 51fe1ea3feacb931cd66b0f915b046cbeab88790 first introduced both halves in one non-squash commit: it preserved test-capable inputs as matchers and invoked their test method on allowed-claim values. Its immediate parent lacks the verifier file entirely, proving direct-parent absence. Later commits only preserved or adjusted the mechanism, so selecting them would misclassify a refactor/fix as the BIC. The BIC is an ancestor of the advisory's first affected tag v5.0.0. The advisory-designated direct fix b0be0ca161593836a153d5180ca5358ad9b5de94 is absent from v6.2.0 and is the direct parent of the v6.2.1 release commit, matching the published boundary, although source review shows the landed behavior warns rather than prevents evaluation. Finally, the BIC commit object has a human author/committer and no AI/bot marker or AI trailer. Under BIC-only attribution, the result is therefore NOT_AI.
